entries.final_answer: Refuse non-finite numbers: serialisation uses allow_nan=False and a NaN/Infinity value refuses as StoreError naming the event, with nothing written. Write LF line endings on every OS by opening the temp file with newline set to LF; the red-first test asserts the newline argument of the temp-file open (CPython on Linux cannot observe CRLF), plus a portable byte pin with no CRLF. After the fix the serialised line equals the spec-kitty-events byte rule.
options: Refuse non-finite numbers (allow_nan=False, refusal as StoreError, nothing written) and write LF-only on every OS (newline="\n"); red test asserts the temp file newline

entries.final_answer: One shared locator in the core layer used by the dependency guard, the subtask roster and the WP view: WP id matched case-insensitively with the existing separator tail, README excluded case-insensitively (the spec-kitty-events R26 rule). A match that is not a regular file (directory, dangling link) makes the gate readers fail closed (roster: SubtaskRosterResolutionError; dependency read: unresolvable TransitionError) and the read-only view/mirror treat it as no file. Other locators (dependency_graph, task_utils/support, workspace/context) are a follow-up.

entries.final_answer: Refuse: the roster accepts only string or integer (not boolean) entries; anything else, and an integer too long to convert (more than 4300 digits), raises SubtaskRosterResolutionError naming the WP file and the expected list form (e.g. '- T001'). entries.final_answer: Build the set of known conflict ids once before the resolved-event pass and add each newly appended id to it, so a repeated resolved event still yields one conflict (dedup preserved). Proof is deterministic: a characterisation test for repeated resolved ids and a scale test asserting 2n conflicts for n requested plus n resolved. No wall-clock performance test; before/after timings are recorded in the PR body.
options: Hoist the existing-id set out of the loop and add each appended id, preserving de-duplication; deterministic tests only, timings recorded in the PR
